title: Rast resists Müller to win Brands Hatch Race 2 as Audi takes the top four places
dek: René Rast converted pole into victory by 0.240 seconds from Audi team-mate Nico Müller in Race 2 at Brands Hatch, in an Audi 1-2-3-4 that extended his title lead.

chapters.title: BMW’s Saturday win, Audi’s answer to come
text: Saturday had gone to BMW. Marco Wittmann won Race 1 from pole by 0.374 seconds from René Rast, after Paul di Resta’s Aston Martin led the opening 14 laps until a five-second jump-start penalty dropped him back. Nico Müller was third, and Rast kept the championship lead on 178 points.
Sunday’s race was on a dry track, the second qualifying session having been held that morning. Pietro Fittipaldi had missed Race 1 after his qualifying crash, but WRT rebuilt his Audi overnight.

chapters.title: Rast’s fifth pole of the year as Audi fills the first four rows
text: Audi dominated Sunday’s qualifying. Rast led after the first runs with a 1m15.696s, then returned in the final five minutes and improved by more than half a second to 1m15.134s, his fifth pole of the season. His benchmark was never threatened, and Audi locked out the top eight places on the grid.

Duval improved late to take second on 1m15.432s, and Robin Frijns, who had the earlier best, ended third on 1m15.834s. Jamie Green was fourth, Mike Rockenfeller fifth and Müller sixth, the title challenger saying afterwards that he needed to improve his qualifying. Fittipaldi was seventh on 1m16.015s, only 0.001 seconds ahead of WRT team-mate Jonathan Aberdein.

Philipp Eng was the best BMW in ninth and Daniel Juncadella the best Aston Martin in tenth. Timo Glock was 11th, and Wittmann, who had topped the times after the first runs, tumbled to 12th. Di Resta, who had qualified so well on Saturday, was 15th, and Ferdinand Habsburg was last on the grid in 18th.

chapters.title: Duval beats Rast to the first corner, Rast takes it back
text: Rast made a poor getaway for the second day running, and Duval beat him to Paddock Hill Bend from the front row. Rast was back in front by the end of the first lap, passing Duval on the run to Hawthorns. Green was handed a five-second penalty for the position of his car on the grid, which pushed him out of the front-running group.

Müller, starting sixth, made up places at the start and then repeated Rast’s move on Duval to take second. That set up the fight for the win, with the two championship rivals separated by a little over a second when the first stops approached.

chapters.title: A slow stop for Müller, and a slow zone that helps BMW
text: Rast and Müller pitted together in the first third of the race. Rast’s stop was clean, but a problem fitting the rear-left tyre on Müller’s Audi cost him about five seconds. He returned in a net second place, 3.3 seconds behind, once he had cleared Frijns and Duval, who were still on their out-laps.

Strategy split the field. Eng stayed out for a long first stint and made his stop on lap 22. Joel Eriksson’s BMW stopped on the circuit just after the start-finish line, which brought a slow zone that helped Eng and Wittmann. Wittmann, who had started 12th, attempted a two-stop plan, but the gamble did not pay off. Dennis ran a long first stint to climb from 17th on the grid, and Di Resta’s long first stint was undone by a slow stop.

chapters.title: Müller closes to 0.240 seconds at the flag
text: Once everyone had stopped Rast led Müller by about a second. Müller set a series of fast laps over the second half of the race and closed to 0.240 seconds at the line, but never found a way past, and Rast took his fourth win of the season. Frijns was 0.598 seconds behind in third and Duval fourth, 2.362 seconds off the winner, completing an Audi 1-2-3-4.

Behind them, Eng and Rockenfeller fought for fifth. Eng passed Rockenfeller on the inside at Surtees, then found Duval a tougher proposition. The pair made slight contact at Surtees and ran side by side on the way to Hawthorns, but Eng could not get by and finished fifth, 2.889 seconds off the win. Rockenfeller was sixth, van der Linde seventh after avoiding Aberdein’s spinning Audi, Juncadella eighth and Dennis ninth, so Aston Martin scored with two cars. Wittmann was tenth.

Habsburg was 11th ahead of Glock, with Aberdein 13th, Di Resta 14th and Green 15th after his penalty. Fittipaldi was 16th and set the fastest lap, a 1m18.169s on lap 27. Spengler and Eriksson both retired.

chapters.title: Rast leads Müller by 37 points as BMW looks for an answer
text: Rast’s victory, his fourth of the season, came with pole and gave him the maximum 28 points of the day. He said he had to shuffle his tyre sets because gravel in the pit lane had damaged one set after qualifying, but that the Hankook race tyres held up well for the whole race and let him defend his lead. Müller said his car had a better balance than on Saturday, which made tyre management easier, and that he was happy with his weekend. Frijns said Brands Hatch rewarded drivers who looked after their tyres, and that he had managed 27 laps on one set on Saturday and 29 on Sunday.

The championship picture moved Rast’s way. He left Brands Hatch on 206 points, 37 clear of Müller on 169, with Wittmann third on 147 after scoring a single point on Sunday and Eng fourth on 129. The three remaining weekends, six races in all, still had plenty of points to offer, and Hankook’s motorsport director called Rast the favourite going into the final third of the season.

BMW’s director of motorsport Jens Marquardt called Wittmann’s Saturday win magnificent but said Sunday’s qualifying made it clear that “you have to qualify higher up the grid” to turn race pace into results. He praised Eng’s fifth place and said BMW would examine why it had not qualified better before the next round. The Saturday result also carried a cost: the three best-placed BMW finishers in Race 1, Wittmann, Eng and van der Linde, did not count towards BMW’s manufacturers’ total because of the extra engine seals.

Aston Martin took two cars into the points at its home round, with Juncadella eighth and Dennis ninth, which Dennis called great for a DTM newcomer at its home race. Di Resta, who had led on Saturday, finished 14th after a slow first-stint stop. Audi had taken the top four places on the day. The DTM now moves on to the Lausitzring on 24–25 August.

facts.v: Rast, Müller, Frijns and Duval finished 1-2-3-4 for Audi, with Eng the best BMW in fifth.
